did: Tested live in the browser pane by hand. The owner published a post from Karim Pharmacy: "Moderator needed for our Facebook page" (kind: Need a worker) with a contact line. A different signed-in person (a student) opened it, read how to reach the poster, and left a comment saying they can do it.

checks.text: The post shows its title, the words, the 'how to reach them' line ("Call 01700000003 after 6 pm") and the notice that the board is only a place to meet
A signed-in stranger could comment ("I can do this. I am a student and free every evening after 6 pm. Please call me.") and the comment appeared at once with its date and time
A guest sees the post but is told to log in before they can see how to reach the poster and before commenting

notes: Done by hand in the live browser. While testing, a comment that was refused showed its message at the very top of the page, away from the comment box. Fixed: the refusal now shows right above the Comment button.

shots.caption: A student reads the moderator post and how to reach the poster
Their comment is on the post
A guest is asked to log in to see how to reach them
